note: Simple Timeline is a single Views style plugin (id simple_timeline, class SimpleTimeline extending StylePluginBase, theme views_view_simple_timeline). It has no settings form, no configure route, no permissions, no Drush. Its only persistent state is a view display's style config: views.view.<id> -> display.<display>.display_options.style.{type, options}. The four options are position_items (alternate/left/right), position_marker (marker-top/marker-center/marker-bottom), wrapper_class (default wrapper-list) and class (default item-list). medium/hard cases create namespaced views (st_*) with base_table node_field_data and read/write the style config; cleanup deletes the view.

evals.prompt: How do I display a Drupal view as a vertical timeline using the simple_timeline module? What kind of plugin does it provide and how do I use it?
evals.expected_output: It provides a Views style plugin 'simple_timeline' ('Simple Timeline'). In a view choose Format -> Simple Timeline; the rows are then rendered on a vertical timeline.

evals.prompt: In the simple_timeline views style, how can I control whether items appear on the left, right, or alternate around the timeline line? Which option key controls that and what are its values?
evals.expected_output: The style option position_items controls it, with values alternate (default), left, or right.

evals.prompt: In the simple_timeline module, which option sets the marker's vertical position, and how do I change the timeline line colour or the marker's look?
evals.expected_output: position_marker (marker-top / marker-center / marker-bottom) sets the marker's vertical position. Colours/shapes are changed with CSS in your theme, e.g. `ul.timeline-list:after { background-color: ... }` for the line and `span.timeline-marker { ... }` for the marker.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a view named 'st_demo' that renders its rows with the Simple Timeline style. Inspect the live view configuration and state how its items are positioned relative to the timeline (alternate, left, or right).
evals.expected_output: position_items is 'left'. Read it from views.view.st_demo default display: display_options.style.options.position_items.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site a view named 'st_marker' uses the Simple Timeline style. Inspect the live configuration and state where the marker is positioned on each row (top, center, or bottom).
evals.expected_output: position_marker is 'marker-bottom'. Read it from views.view.st_marker default display: display_options.style.options.position_marker.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a view with machine name 'st_task' whose default display currently uses the default (unformatted list) style. Using the simple_timeline module, change that display's format to the Simple Timeline style. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set the st_task view's default display style type to 'simple_timeline' (views.view.st_task -> display.default.display_options.style.type = simple_timeline).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the view 'st_pos' already uses the Simple Timeline style with items alternating around the line. Change it so all items are positioned to the right of the timeline. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set the st_pos view's Simple Timeline style option position_items to 'right' (keeping style type simple_timeline).
